title: Does Parenthood Really Ruin Couples’ Sex Lives?
gist: Wendy Wang uses 2021–2024 General Social Survey data to show parenthood is not a significant predictor of a sexless marriage; age, low family income and low religious attendance are. Sex frequency among married Americans has fallen sharply (weekly sex 61% in the 1990s to 46%), with the steepest decline among childless couples under 50.

insights.claim: Among prime-age married U.S. adults (25–64), childless and parent groups now report similar rates of weekly sex, ending a long-standing edge for childless couples; childless adults are slightly more likely to report no or almost no sex in the past year (17% vs. 15%), per 2021–2024 GSS data.
insights.speaker: Wendy Wang
insights.so_what: Undercuts a common narrative that children are a relationship cost, relevant to fertility-decision framing.
